text: I had a chief of staff who I was lucky to  work with for a year named Kimberly Cotton,
and she was the chief of staff to the  CEO of this Fortune 500 company. I met
her backstage speaking at a large event for  that company. Turns out her CEO was retiring.
Anyway, to make a long story short,  she was a master question asker,
and she illuminated for me something that I  had experienced over my life, which is there
are three types of questions that you can ask  someone that really actually make a difference,
that help shape or edit the future in some  way. And so, in this video, I’m going to
give you what I believe are three way better  conversation starters that maybe could replace
all icebreakers. And I’m going to get really  close and intense to share these three framings.
At one level, you can ask possibility questions,  right? What is possible? Sharing a vision for what
is possible in the future. On the next  level, you ask process questions. It’s
a little bit more digging into the how—how  do you actually wind up there? And then Kim
was amazing at asking practical questions. So I  would share this vision or an idea for something,
and she was a master of saying, “That’s amazing.  By when would you like to have that done?”
So let me give you three questions that I  really love that you can walk someone through,
right from possibility into process  into a very practical place. You ready?
At the possibility level of questions,  you’re really talking about vision,
right? Getting someone’s larger aim. It doesn’t  need to be hyper-specific. You’re just like, “What
do you want?” Right? Those kinds of questions. If  I ask you a question like, “If you could solve one
problem in the world, what would it be?” And  so when I hear somebody’s response to that,
what I’m now getting curious about—if I’m  kind of hovering—I almost picture these
possibility, process, and practical levels  like a spiral, where you’ve got to start
in the land of possibility, in the land of  why, what’s the point, what’s the big vision.
Otherwise, what happens too often is  when we try to get action-oriented,
we ask practical questions. Practical questions  are great at generating a bunch of activity that
leads to nowhere because they’re not tied to  some larger vision. And so, when you start with
the level of possibility and you spiral down  to how it’s going to get done—process—when I
ask you a question like, “What brings you joy?”  and then I’m able to combine that with, “Okay,
you want to solve this problem, and what brings  you joy?” I can now start to think, how do those
intersect? How might you combine those? So there’s  some reflection and debriefing happening there.
And then, really practically, what is it that you
want to start doing? So you can see  this is just three question examples.
I got so on about this idea that questions  are the edit button to the future, that
questions that are future-focused spark  the tiny actions, which is us verbalizing,
us creating new neural pathways that lead to  actual implementation out in the world. And so
what I did was spend a whole heap of time packing  60 possibility, process, and practical questions
into what I believe is the coolest tool to replace  all other icebreakers or conversation starters.
It is the Future-Focused We  Connect Cards, and it’s really
simply a deck designed to help people talk their  way into a more compelling, interesting tomorrow.
The no-prep takeaway here is that when you’re  in a group, if you can start with possibility
questions as a conversation starter, and then take  their answers to that and add a process-oriented
question like, “How do you like going about that?”  and then drop it into really practical terms like,
“What’s the tiniest action you might want to  take in the next week to make that happen?”—that
sequence of possibility to process to  practical is transformative for a group.
And so, if you want to start conversations that  actually go somewhere, that make a difference,
that is your formula. If you want to pick up a  deck of these cards, they’re available on the
internet. I guess they’re sponsoring this  video. I don’t know. Have an awesome day.
